info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package security is secret scanning for your code: submit sources, get findings, masked never raw.

get.summary: Is the org's findings — rule, severity, path, line, masked preview and fingerprint — newest first, across scans or within one.
get.description:
Is the org's findings — rule, severity, path, line, masked preview
and fingerprint — newest first, across scans or within one.

A minSeverity outside critical|high|medium|low is refused rather than quietly
ignored, so a filter typo cannot read as "no findings". Strictly org-scoped, and
a caller with no validated org is refused.

parameters.name: scanId
parameters.description: ScanID narrows to a single scan.

parameters.name: minSeverity
parameters.description:
MinSeverity drops everything below that rank: critical, high, medium or low.
A value outside that set is refused rather than quietly ignored, so a filter
typo cannot read as "no findings".

get.summary: Returns a single finding: which rule fired, where (path and line), the masked preview and the SHA-256 fingerprint of the secret — the raw secret is not stored and cannot be read back.
get.description:
Returns a single finding: which rule fired, where (path and line),
the masked preview and the SHA-256 fingerprint of the secret — the raw secret is
not stored and cannot be read back.

Scoped to the caller's org, and a finding belonging to another org is the same
404 as one that never existed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the finding the URL names.

get.summary: Reports that the scanning subsystem is serving and how many secret-detection rules the engine holds.
get.description:
Reports that the scanning subsystem is serving and how many
secret-detection rules the engine holds.

It has no external dependency — the answer is ok whenever the findings store
opened — so it measures this process rather than anything downstream. It reads
no tenant: a prober that sends no principal is answered, not refused.

get.summary: Is the secret-detection catalog the engine scans with.
get.description:
Is the secret-detection catalog the engine scans with.

It returns every rule a scan can fire — the id, name and severity a finding
cites — so a caller can render or triage results without hard-coding the
catalog. It is the same for everyone and discloses nothing tenant-specific, so
it carries no org scope.

get.summary: Is the org's scan history, newest first, each as the same summary the submission answered — files read, findings fired, tally by severity.
get.description:
Is the org's scan history, newest first, each as the same summary the
submission answered — files read, findings fired, tally by severity.

Strictly org-scoped: a caller only ever sees its own scans, and one with no
validated org is refused.

post.summary: Runs the detection engine over a batch of files and answers 201 with the scan summary: how many files were read, how many findings fired, and the tally by severity.
post.description:
Runs the detection engine over a batch of files and answers 201 with
the scan summary: how many files were read, how many findings fired, and the
tally by severity.

THE SUBMITTED CONTENT IS NEVER STORED. It is scanned in memory; what persists is
the finding — its rule, its path and line, a MASKED preview (first and last
characters kept, the middle starred) and the SHA-256 fingerprint of the raw
secret. The fingerprint is what makes the same secret recognisable across scans
and after rotation without the secret ever being written down.

It requires a validated org, which scopes the stored scan and every finding on
it; a caller with no org is refused. Bounded at 500 files and 8 MiB of total
content per submission — split a larger tree across scans. One scan is one
metered unit, and the scan is recorded in the audit log with its tally, never
with its findings.

get.summary: Returns one scan together with every finding on it, so the detail view is one round-trip rather than a list call per scan.
get.description:
Returns one scan together with every finding on it, so the detail view
is one round-trip rather than a list call per scan. The findings carry masked
previews and fingerprints, never secrets.

Scoped to the caller's org: a scan id belonging to another org is the same 404
as an id that never existed, so a ruleset learns nothing about what exists
elsewhere. No validated org is refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the scan the URL names.

description.description: what kind of secret this rule recognises

id.description: the rule identifier a finding cites

severity.description: how serious a match is: critical, high, medium or low

data.description: Data is the caller org's findings, newest first.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the finding was recorded, in Unix milliseconds.

fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the raw secret. It is what makes the same
secret recognisable across scans and after rotation without the secret ever
being written down.

line.description: Line is where in that file.

path.description: Path is the file the secret was found in.

preview.description:
Preview is the secret MASKED — first and last characters kept, the middle
starred — so a reviewer can recognise it without it being disclosed.

ruleId.description: RuleID is the detection rule that fired.

ruleName.description: RuleName is that rule's human name.

scanId.description: ScanID is the scan that produced it.

severity.description: Severity ranks the finding: critical, high, medium or low.

data.description:
Data is every rule a scan can fire, each with the id, name and severity a
finding cites.

rules.description: Rules is how many detection rules the engine holds.

status.description: Status is "ok" whenever the findings store opened.

content.description:
Content is the source to scan. It is NEVER stored: what persists is the
finding, with a masked preview and a fingerprint.

path.description:
Path is where the file lives, recorded on any finding so a result can be
located in the tree it came from.

findings.description: Findings is every finding on that scan, so the detail view is one round-trip.

data.description: Data is the caller org's scans, newest first.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the scan ran, in Unix milliseconds.

critical.description: Critical is how many findings carry the highest severity.

files.description: Files is how many files the scan read.

findings.description: Findings is how many secrets fired across them.

high.description: High is how many findings rank high.

id.description: ID addresses this scan and every finding on it.

low.description: Low is how many findings rank low.

medium.description: Medium is how many findings rank medium.

project.description: Project is the sub-scope the scan was filed under.

files.description: Files is the batch to scan, at most 500 files and 8 MiB of content in total.

project.description:
Project names the sub-scope the scan is filed under. It must be a slug; omit
it and the caller's project header is used instead.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
